model_annotation: Figure 4 is a bar chart titled “Number of participants (N = 6) who highlighted each evaluation criterion as beneficial,” illustrating the frequency with which six participants selected specific criteria as beneficial features of the evaluated tool. The horizontal axis lists the evaluation criteria in the order: “retrieval of relevant fact-checks (FCs),” “concise summaries,” “explanations,” and “clarity of the interface.” The vertical axis represents the count of participants, scaled linearly from 0 to 6, with tick marks at intervals of 1, indicating the number of participants who selected each criterion. The chart contains four vertical bars, each corresponding to one criterion, colored uniformly in dark gray. The bar for “retrieval of relevant fact-checks (FCs)” is the tallest, reaching a value of 6, indicating all six participants found this criterion beneficial. The bar for “concise summaries” is the second tallest, reaching a value of 5. The bar for “explanations” reaches a value of 4, and the bar for “clarity of the interface” reaches a value of 3. There is no indication that the bars are sorted, and no visual emphasis such as shading or outlines is applied to any of the bars.
